item.title: The road to revitalizing Pleasanton’s Main Street
item.description: Strolling through downtown Pleasanton, it’s hard for many to look past the vacant storefronts — seemingly one a block, if not more; some deserted for years, while others emptied only recently. But the PDA says plenty is going on behind the scenes in those units and elsewhere in and around Main Street to set the stage for an exciting, vibrant 2026 downtown. The post The road to revitalizing Pleasanton’s Main Street appeared first on Pleasanton Weekly.

item.description: Pleasanton native Sean Mannion continues his quick ascent up the National Football League coaching ranks after a nine-year playing career, being named as the new offensive coordinator for the Philadelphia Eagles on Thursday. item.title: More small earthquakes shake Tri-Valley
item.description: A handful of small earthquakes have been recorded in the Tri-Valley in recent days, with the largest measured at magnitude 3.4 on Friday morning, per USGS. The post More small earthquakes shake Tri-Valley appeared first on Pleasanton Weekly.

item.title: Dublin council instates 45-day prohibition against new firearms retailers
item.description: Dublin has entered into a temporary moratorium on the establishment of new firearms retailers and shooting ranges, as well as their expansion or relocation, with the City Council hitting the pause button after an inquiry from a prospective dealer who might want to open near a future school site. The post Dublin council instates 45-day prohibition against new firearms retailers appeared first on Pleasanton Weekly.

item.title: Supervisors approve ‘ICE-Free Zones’ on Alameda County-controlled properties
item.description: The Alameda County Board of Supervisors voted unanimously this week to approve a pair of ordinances designed to help shield residents from an increasingly chaotic federal immigration crackdown. item.title: Dublin man convicted of rapes while at UC Santa Barbara
item.description: A young man from Dublin was found guilty of committing multiple sexual assaults while in college, Santa Barbara County prosecutors announced Jan. 20 following a three-month trial that ended with a hung jury on more than a dozen other counts. item.title: Deal reached on $590M loan to prop up Bay Area transit agencies
item.description: State and local officials have agreed on a $590 million bridge loan to prop up Bay Area transit agencies until voters decide on a sales tax increase to bolster the systems.
